 | `POST /content/catalog/pull?scope=` | `{ url, path?, mode?, note? }` | The platform fetches your JSON feed over HTTPS and imports it |
 
+Catalog operations require a typed access/service operator credential granted to the canonical tenant resolved at ingress (for example through `X-Tenant`) in every auth mode. Optional `scope`/`tenant` selectors must match it exactly and appear once. Catalog reads use explicitly initialized R2 publication; there is no compiled-default or legacy-KV fallback. Initialization is a library capability requiring an approved supplied baseline and quiesced old writers; no HTTP endpoint initializes a catalog. Versions below that baseline report `legacy_history_unavailable`.
+
+Catalog PUT, import, pull and rollback require `If-Match: "N"` for the last observed committed revision and `Idempotency-Key: N:UUID` (canonical decimal N and lowercase UUID). Missing headers return 428, invalid input 400/422, stale/conflicting operations 409 and unavailable/corrupt/unconfirmed storage 503. Catalog and head objects are limited to 2 MiB UTF-8 each; version labels to 4096 characters including the new revision suffix. Immutable historical bodies remain individually addressable after they leave the latest-50 index. Rollback writes the historical value forward as a new revision.
+
+`GET /content/catalog/publication` discovers committed revision, historical floor and any pending operation's ID/base/original actor/digest. The same headers optionally inspect a particular operation. After a failed or ambiguous publication, `POST /content/catalog/publication/recover` with its original headers finishes that retained intent, preserving its attribution; another currently granted operator can recover it. It accepts no replacement body and never refetches a feed. Initialization recovery remains library-only. Other writers conflict until the pending operation finishes. Repeating an identical ordinary write returns its retained receipt; pull rejects pending/stale bases before fetching, so use status/recover after an uncertain pull.
+
+Catalog administration bypasses the serving cache. Serving snapshots are immutable, keyed by bucket and tenant, and expire within 30 seconds of the read's start; an already in-flight read may finish later. A verified cached snapshot can serve until expiry, and failures never refresh it or substitute an empty catalog. R2's same-key write rate limit can leave reservation/finalization pending and return 503; status/recovery is required, with no rapid-publication or deployed latency guarantee. This catalog-only contract does not make slots, learning, reflex or a multi-document decision manifest atomic, and does not activate enrichment exports or satisfy customer immediate-effect acceptance.
+
 The reflex configuration, the registry of dimensions and the engine's constants per brand, has the same
 shape under `/config/reflex` (`GET`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `history`, `revisions/{n}`, `validate`,
 `rollback/{n}`); every route requires the operator access token, including merged-patch validation. The tuning page and the learning console are clients of these routes; there is no
 other way to change what the engine does.
